title: The hypertrophy series: artificial vs organical failure
summary: NH distinguishes organic from artificial failure. Artificial muscular failure is stopping because of lactic acid burn before the fibers are truly fatigued, avoided by using rep ranges heavy enough that the burn arrives at or after the end of the set. Artificial mechanical failure is unintended form breakdown, while organic mechanical failure is a deliberately disadvantaged position, like a crane-style stiff-leg deadlift, used to target a muscle.
claims: Artificial muscular failure is when lactic acid burn stops the set even though the muscle fibers are not truly exhausted
People differ in lactic acid production; some produce much less and can push further
You can push through lactic acid fatigue with mindset only so far, because it is engineered to make the muscle stop
Artificial failure is not the best for hypertrophy
Choose rep ranges challenging enough that the lactic acid response kicks in after the set or only in the last few reps; most sets should be like that
Pump work in the 30-40 rep range is not a good way to grow as a natural; focus on lower rep ranges where you can push strength and progression
A few sets of artificial failure here and there are acceptable but should not be the focus because they limit tonnage
Artificial mechanical failure happens unintentionally through poor technique or bar placement and can be corrected so it never recurs

Organic mechanical failure is a position you choose that is mechanically weak, such as a stiff-leg deadlift with the bar near the toes lifted like a crane, to make the hamstrings reach muscular failure faster
If you know how to create mechanical failure, you know how to avoid it; it is an advanced concept
exercises: bar near the toes, lift like a crane
deliberate mechanical disadvantage to target hamstrings
